t: Starting from his father's jagir at Pune, Shivaji took Bijapuri forts from 1647 and built a state between the Deccan sultanates and the Mughal Empire.
He alternated between war and vassalage with the Mughals, sacking Surat in 1664 and 1670, submitting at Purandar in 1665 and escaping house arrest at Agra in 1666.
Crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674 despite the objection of Brahmins that he was not a Kshatriya, he has since been claimed by reformers, nationalists and Hindutva activists in turn.
dyk: Shivaji replaced Persian with Marathi at his court and had his official Raghunath Pandit compile the Rājavyavahārakośa (1677), a thesaurus replacing Persian and Arabic terms of state with Sanskrit ones.
ev: Shivaji, aged 16, captures Torna Fort and uses its treasure to build Rajgad
He kills the Bijapuri general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad and defeats his army
Shivaji sacks the Mughal port of Surat
By the Treaty of Purandar he gives up 23 forts and becomes a Mughal vassal
Placed under house arrest at Agra, he escapes with his son Sambhaji
Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad Fort
He invades Karnataka and takes Vellore and Gingee

f.born: c. 19 February 1630 (scholars disagree on the date) at the hill-fort of Shivneri near Junnar; son of the Maratha general Shahaji Bhonsle and Jijabai
f.died: around 3-5 April 1680 at Raigad Fort, after an illness with fever and dysentery; the cause is disputed
f.role: Holder of the Pune jagir from 1647; Mughal vassal under the Treaty of Purandar, 1665; Raja by Mughal grant, 1666-1668; Chhatrapati of the Maratha Kingdom, 1674-1680
f.known: founding the Maratha Kingdom; the killing of Afzal Khan at Pratapgad; the sacks of Surat; escape from Agra; coronation at Raigad; hill forts and the Maratha navy; the Ashta Pradhan council
